output.summary: I added a middle tier to TrySetExactBloomFilter in physical_hash_join.cpp. A join filter can now use the exact bitmap when the key range is below min(2^27 bits, which is 16MB, and count×1024 bits). The existing 128 bits/key rule, the 2^22 small-range floor and the 2^32 max guard are unchanged. The multiplication only happens when count ≤ 2^17, so it can't overflow; above that the 2^27 cap applies directly. I also updated the comment about memory. Exact-bitmap building, probing and the CM offset path already handle ranges up to 2^32, so nothing else changed. Build OK and result checks passed. Bench against best across 3 runs: q05 -9.1%, -18.3%, -20.5%. q04 went -14.8%, +14.2%, +1.0%, and q09 went +11.0%, +1.7%, +2.0%; both swing both ways, so I read them as noise. The first full-suite run had a geomean of -1.8%, with q03 -6% and q16 -5% there. I did not profile q05, so I haven't confirmed directly that its lineitem filter is now exact or that scan CPU fell to about 0.48s. The consistent q05 gain fits the hypothesis.
output.generality: This helps FK joins where a filtered build side (a dimension or fact filtered by date or segment) has integer keys spread thinly (128 to 1024 bits per key) over a range of up to about 134M. The probe-side scan then does one bit test per row instead of hashing, and there are no false positives. It does not apply to non-integer keys, ranges of 2^27 or more with fewer than 128 bits per key, or NULL-equal joins. Possible downside: probe keys in random order against a 4–16MB bitmap could miss L3 more often than a hashed BF would. There is also a one-time cost of zeroing up to 16MB per join.
output.notes: The only gain I saw consistently is q05. q04 and q09 swung between -15% and +14% across reruns, which is bench noise. Worth checking in the full timing run that q09 does not regress. Follow-up idea: a sparse two-level or blocked exact bitmap for ranges above 2^27.
